currency.basis: The kit zip is dated 2025-09-12 and uses the current brand purple #533AFD of Stripe's recent rebrand; it is the media kit the official newsroom page currently offers for download.

identity.basis: The wordmark 'stripe' in the official logo kit is Stripe's own brand asset served from stripeassets.com via the official newsroom page; lowercase stripe letterforms are unmistakable.

assessment.independenceRationale: Single official source (newsroom kit); the favicon from the same official asset domain corroborates the #533AFD brand color.

variant.basis: Blurple wordmark variant selected from the official kit (slate/white variants also present); wordmark is the variant the accepted icon also presents, and letters forming the mark are allowed for catalog suitability.

candidate.detailsJudgement: All letter strokes, counters and the t-crossbar survive conversion and optimization; the rsvg source reference and the offscreen final renders show identical shapes with no lost detail or artifacts.
candidate.proportionsJudgement: The 360x150 wordmark is uniformly scaled into the square cell; at 240x240 the mark spans the icon area with comfortable margins and stays legible at 24/32/48 px diagnostics; no stretching or cropping.
candidate.rationale: Stripe's official newsroom logo kit (2025-09-12) serves the current wordmark in the new brand purple #533AFD; the accepted icon uses the legacy blurple circle with the older wordmark letterforms. This is a documented rebrand of the same bank, so the update replaces obsolete branding rather than normalizing bytes.
candidate.role: Standalone wordmark: lowercase 'stripe' letterforms are the mark itself, without any accompanying slogan or explanatory text.
transforms: No geometry transformation was needed: the whole wordmark viewBox 0 0 360 150 is kept unchanged with only whole-emblem uniform scaling/centering by the catalog renderer.

SVGO 4.1.0 with the repository frozen svgo.config.mjs (config bound to baseCommit) reduced the working copy from 2139 to 1459 bytes; the optimized trial was pixel-identical (PIL ImageChops difference bbox None) and was selected as final.svg.
candidate.variant: Blurple (#533AFD) wordmark variant selected from the official kit; the slate and white variants were not used. The wordmark is presented transparent on the catalog cell, matching the same transparent presentation of the downloaded official SVG.
candidate.visibleDiffExplanation: Base is a legacy blurple circle containing the older white wordmark; the candidate is the current official wordmark in brand purple #533AFD without the circle backing. The difference is the evidenced Stripe rebrand plus presentation without the circular backing of the old asset.

proposals.reason: Stripe rebranded: the accepted icon uses the legacy blurple (#6772E5-style) circle with the older wordmark, while Stripe's official newsroom media kit (zip dated 2025-09-12) serves the current wordmark in the new brand purple #533AFD. The fetched member 'asset-wordmark/Stripe wordmark - Blurple.svg' is an original official vector (pure paths, viewBox 0 0 360 150). The official favicon.svg rounded-square variant contains only a bare white parallelogram and is not a recognizable standalone mark, so the official wordmark is the evidenced replacement. This is a documented rebrand of the same bank, not an identity dispute.

sourceCandidate.rationale: Official original-vector wordmark in the current brand color #533AFD replaces the accepted legacy-color (#6772E5-style) wordmark icon; evidenced rebrand plus updated letterforms.

sources.observation: Official Stripe newsroom media-assets page offers 'Download logo kit' with blurple/slate/white wordmark variants and a Marks Usage Agreement; the zip (sha256 30f4308c21a8f6c3fe603354ce69222fd498afeb80f54fda193fb7291208906f) contains the blurple wordmark SVG (#533AFD) with current letterforms.

Official favicon.svg is a #533AFD rounded square whose only foreground element is a white parallelogram; inspected as a rendered image it is not a recognizable standalone Stripe mark, so it was rejected as candidate material.
